37@triton.jit 

38def _next_below(x, DT: tl.constexpr): 

39 """Largest ``DT`` value strictly less than ``x``. 

40 

41 Used to build the exclusive upper bound of the sampling interval in the 

42 *output* dtype: ``uniform`` samples from ``[from, to)``, so a value that 

43 rounds up to ``to`` in a low-precision dtype must be stepped back one ulp. 

44 

45 A zero input needs care: the bit patterns of ``+0.0`` and ``-0.0`` are the 

46 bottom of the positive block and the top of the negative block, so the 

47 usual "-1 for x >= 0, +1 otherwise" step walks *out* of the number line and 

48 wraps around -- ``+0.0`` (0) minus one is all-ones, and ``-0.0`` 

49 (0x8000...0) plus one is all-ones too, both of which are NaN. The true 

50 predecessor of either zero is ``-smallest_subnormal``, so a zero input is 

51 answered directly as the negation of the smallest positive subnormal. 

52 """ 

53 zero = x == 0 

54 if DT == tl.float32: 

55 bits = x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) 

56 step = tl.where(x >= 0, -1, 1).to(tl.int32) 

57 stepped = (bits + step).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) 

58 # smallest positive subnormal: the bit pattern with a lone low bit. 

59 tiny = tl.full((), 1, tl.int32).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) 

60 return tl.where(zero, -tiny, stepped).to(tl.float32) 

61 elif DT == tl.float64: 

62 bits = x.to(tl.int64, bitcast=True) 

63 step = tl.where(x >= 0, -1, 1).to(tl.int64) 

64 stepped = (bits + step).to(tl.float64, bitcast=True) 

65 tiny = tl.full((), 1, tl.int64).to(tl.float64, bitcast=True) 

66 return tl.where(zero, -tiny, stepped).to(tl.float64) 

67 else: 

68 bits = x.to(tl.int16, bitcast=True) 

69 step = tl.where(x >= 0, -1, 1).to(tl.int16) 

70 stepped = (bits + step).to(DT, bitcast=True) 

71 tiny = tl.full((), 1, tl.int16).to(DT, bitcast=True) 

72 return tl.where(zero, -tiny, stepped).to(DT)

75@triton.jit 

76def _mix32(x): 

77 """Murmur3-style 32-bit finalizer, reduced to one mixing round. 

78 

79 Ascend's vector unit has no cheap integer XOR: a ``^`` on 32-bit lanes 

80 lowers to a long instruction sequence and measures ~5x the cost of the 

81 equivalent ``(a | b) - (a & b)`` (0.039 ms vs 0.007 ms for 2^24 lanes), 

82 which is why the emulation is used here and why the classic three-xor 

83 finalizer is too slow for this kernel (~0.24 ms against ~0.10 ms for a 

84 single mixing round on a 16M-element fp32 fill, with a ~0.02 ms memory 

85 floor). One xor-shift between two odd multiplies keeps the statistical 

86 quality (2-D pair chi-square within noise of a reference PRNG, unlike a 

87 multiply-only hash, which leaves the samples on a lattice). 

88 

89 Both the emulated XOR and the shifted operand are masked so that arithmetic 

90 right shifts (how this backend lowers ``>>``) cannot smear the sign bit into 

91 the high bits. 

92 """ 

93 x = x * 0x7FEB352D 

94 t = (x >> 16) & 0x0000FFFF 

95 x = (x | t) - (x & t) 

96 x = x * 0x846CA68B 

97 return x

100@triton.jit 

101def _uint_to_unit_float(x): 

102 """Hashed counter -> float in [0, 1). 

103 

104 Forcing the exponent of 23 mantissa bits is equivalent to 

105 ``uint_to_uniform_float`` on this range but costs one AND plus one OR 

106 instead of a compare/select abs plus a multiply. The *low* 23 bits are 

107 used, not the high ones: Ascend lowers ``uint32 >>`` as an arithmetic 

108 shift, so extracting the top bits would need an extra mask after the shift 

109 (an unmasked high-bit extraction sets the exponent to all ones and yields 

110 NaN), and the low bits of a mixed counter are just as well distributed 

111 (2-D pair chi-square 4738 against 6293 for the shifted form). 

112 """ 

113 return ((x & 0x007FFFFF) | 0x3F800000).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) - 1.0

116@triton.jit 

117def fast_uniform4x(seed, philox_offset, offset): 

118 """Draw four uniform [0, 1) blocks from a block of counters ``offset``. 

119 

120 Used instead of :func:`uniform` on devices where ``tl.philox`` is 

121 pathologically slow: Philox needs ten rounds of ``umulhi`` chains, and on 

122 Ascend that runs ~20x slower than the memory traffic it accompanies. This 

123 hash only needs 32-bit low multiplies while still producing well-mixed, 

124 independent streams. 

125 

126 ``seed`` and ``philox_offset`` (the generator state) are folded into the 

127 key so that consecutive launches draw different values, and the counter is 

128 scaled by the stream count so the four streams never share an input. 

129 """ 

130 key = seed.to(tl.uint32) ^ (philox_offset.to(tl.uint32) * 0x1E3779B1) 

131 base = offset.to(tl.uint32) * 4 + key 

132 r0 = _uint_to_unit_float(_mix32(base)) 

133 r1 = _uint_to_unit_float(_mix32(base + 1)) 

134 r2 = _uint_to_unit_float(_mix32(base + 2)) 

135 r3 = _uint_to_unit_float(_mix32(base + 3)) 

136 return r0, r1, r2, r3 

137

139@triton.jit 

140def _unit_stream(seed, philox_offset, i): 

141 """One uniform [0, 1) sample per element of the offset tile ``i``. 

142 

143 The element offset doubles as the counter, so a launch consumes exactly one 

144 counter per sample and neighbouring samples (i.e. neighbouring lanes of the 

145 same stream) use neighbouring counters -- the best-mixed case for the 

146 counter hash. 

147 """ 

148 key = seed.to(tl.uint32) ^ (philox_offset.to(tl.uint32) * 0x1E3779B1) 

149 return _uint_to_unit_float(_mix32(i.to(tl.uint32) + key))

153# the random operators generate. Those operators pass ``FAST_RNG`` as a 

154# constexpr and use :func:`fast_uniform4x` instead of Philox. 

155FAST_RNG_VENDORS = ("ascend",)

158def use_fast_rng(): 

159 """Whether this vendor should use :func:`fast_uniform4x`.""" 

160 return flag_gems.vendor_name in FAST_RNG_VENDORS

163def _uniform_heuristics(): 

164 """Shared ``uniform`` heuristics, with the block capped on venders whose 

165 on-chip buffer cannot hold a ``4 x BLOCK`` fp32 tile (Ascend's 196 KB UB). 

166 """ 

167 config = dict(runtime.get_heuristic_config("uniform")) 

168 backend_block = config["BLOCK"] 

169 

170 def block(args): 

171 value = backend_block(args) 

172 if flag_gems.vendor_name == "ascend": 

173 # 4096 is the widest lane that still fits the on-chip buffer once 

174 # the compiler's multi-buffering is applied (a 8192-lane chain of 

175 # hash temporaries asks for 288 KB against 192 KB and fails to 

176 # compile). Tiny tensors keep the small tile to avoid wasted lanes. 

177 if args["N"] > 4096: 

178 value = 4096 

179 else: 

180 value = min(value, 4096) 

181 return value 

182 

183 config["BLOCK"] = block 

184 return config

187@triton.heuristics(_uniform_heuristics()) 

188@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["philox_seed", "philox_offset"]) 

189def uniform_kernel( 

190 out_ptr, 

191 N, 

192 philox_seed, 

193 philox_offset, 

194 from_, 

195 to, 

196 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

197 FAST_RNG: tl.constexpr, 

198 RANGE_IDENTITY: tl.constexpr = False, 

199 NEEDS_CLAMP: tl.constexpr = True, 

200): 

201 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

202 OUT_DT: tl.constexpr = out_ptr.dtype.element_ty 

203 if NEEDS_CLAMP: 

204 # The clamp bound depends only on the interval and the output dtype, so 

205 # a scalar is enough: building it as a BLOCK-wide tile costs extra 

206 # on-chip buffer and overflows the UB for a wide lane. 

207 # Compare in fp32: the backend cannot select bf16 compares. 

208 to_dt = to.to(OUT_DT) 

209 from_dt = from_.to(OUT_DT) 

210 hi = _next_below(to_dt, OUT_DT) 

211 hi = tl.where(to_dt.to(tl.float32) > from_dt.to(tl.float32), hi, to_dt) 

212 # Grid-stride loop: the launch grid is capped (see _MAX_GRID_X). Each 

213 # stream is materialised and stored on its own so only one ``BLOCK`` tile is 

214 # live at a time; keeping the four streams in flight instead needs four times 

215 # the buffer and, with the compiler's multi-buffering applied, overflows the 

216 # 192 KB on-chip buffer (a 4 x 8192 fp32 tile asks for 360 KB and fails to 

217 # compile). 

218 step = tl.num_programs(0) * BLOCK * 4 

219 base = pid * BLOCK * 4 

220 while base < N: 

221 for u in tl.static_range(4): 

222 off = base + u * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

223 if FAST_RNG: 

224 r = _unit_stream(philox_seed, philox_offset, off) 

225 else: 

226 seed64 = philox_seed.to(tl.int64) 

227 offset64 = philox_offset.to(tl.int64) 

228 c0 = (offset64 & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

229 c1 = ((offset64 >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32) 

230 c0 += off.to(tl.uint32) 

231 _O = c0 * 0 

232 r, _r1, _r2, _r3 = tl.philox(seed64, c0, c1, _O, _O) 

233 r = uint_to_uniform_float(r) 

234 if not RANGE_IDENTITY: 

235 r = r * (to - from_) + from_ 

236 # The scaled value is computed in float32 but stored in the output 

237 # dtype, whose rounding can land exactly on the exclusive ``to`` 

238 # bound (notably for float16/bfloat16). Clamp to the output-dtype 

239 # predecessor of ``to`` (``hi``, hoisted above) so sampled values 

240 # stay in ``[from, to)``. 

241 if NEEDS_CLAMP: 

242 r = tl.minimum(r, hi) 

243 tl.store(out_ptr + off, r, mask=off < N, eviction_policy="evict_first") 

244 base += step

247UNROLL = 4 

248# Widest vector lane used for the fill (see _uniform_heuristics). 

249MAX_BLOCK = 4096 

250 

251 

252def _counter_increment(N): 

253 """Upper bound on the Philox counters one launch consumes. 

254 

255 Each program walks ``UNROLL`` streams of ``BLOCK`` counters, so a tail tile 

256 can round the consumed range up past ``N``; reserving the rounded-up range 

257 keeps consecutive launches from re-drawing the same counters. 

258 """ 

259 return N + UNROLL * MAX_BLOCK

262def uniform_(self, from_=0.0, to=1.0, *, generator=None): 

263 logger.debug("GEMS UNIFORM") 

264 N = volume(self.shape) 

265 grid_fn = lambda meta: (min(triton.cdiv(N, meta["BLOCK"] * UNROLL), _MAX_GRID_X),) 

266 

267 increment = _counter_increment(N) 

268 philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset( 

269 increment, generator=generator 

270 ) 

271 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

272 uniform_kernel.run( 

273 self, 

274 N, 

275 philox_seed, 

276 philox_offset, 

277 from_, 

278 to, 

279 FAST_RNG=use_fast_rng(), 

280 RANGE_IDENTITY=(from_ == 0.0 and to == 1.0), 

281 NEEDS_CLAMP=self.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16), 

282 grid=grid_fn, 

283 warmup=False, 

284 ) 

285 return self

288def uniform(self, from_=0.0, to=1.0, *, generator=None): 

289 logger.debug("GEMS UNIFORM") 

290 # aten::uniform rejects an empty interval before launch; mirror that so 

291 # from > to raises instead of silently producing out-of-range values. 

292 if from_ > to: 

293 raise RuntimeError( 

294 "uniform_ expects to return a [from, to) range, but found " 

295 f"from={from_:g} > to={to:g}" 

296 ) 

297 out = torch.empty_like(self) 

298 N = volume(out.shape) 

299 grid_fn = lambda meta: (min(triton.cdiv(N, meta["BLOCK"] * UNROLL), _MAX_GRID_X),) 

300 

301 increment = _counter_increment(N) 

302 philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset( 

303 increment, generator=generator 

304 ) 

305 with torch_device_fn.device(out.device): 

306 uniform_kernel.run( 

307 out, 

308 N, 

309 philox_seed, 

310 philox_offset, 

311 from_, 

312 to, 

313 FAST_RNG=use_fast_rng(), 

314 RANGE_IDENTITY=(from_ == 0.0 and to == 1.0), 

315 NEEDS_CLAMP=out.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16), 

316 grid=grid_fn, 

317 warmup=False, 

318 ) 

319 return out
